clue.text: Stole to secure granny unknown windfall

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn round the shoulders, as is a feather boa
nan is a British family name for a grandmother
Z is one of the letters algebra uses for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone thieved in order to lock in an elderly relative's mysterious stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal but is the noun, a wrap for the shoulders; 'to secure' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean a sudden, unexpected piece of good fortune or large gain.

clue.text: Drab setting for hospital vessel

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what is mounted in it, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: drab and dingy both mean dull and gloomy in colour
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and road signs

explanation.surface: A dull-looking location for a hospital ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small open boat is one kind of craft that sails.

clue.text: Redeploy us with resolve — us, emphatically

indicators.note: to redeploy is to move things into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commander is urged to move the troops with determination, the speaker stressing who is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redeploy' rearranges US and RESOLVE together; 'with' only joins the two. The second 'us' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The emphatic pronoun for the first person plural, as in 'we did it, we and no others'.

clue.text: Withholding name, disdainfully rejects London team

indicators.note: to withhold is to keep something back, so one letter is left out of the word

parts.note: someone who spurns an offer rejects it with contempt

explanation.surface: A football club in the capital turns players down with contempt while refusing to say who.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withholding' takes N out of SPURNS. The team is Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club known by this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the usual nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a football club in the capital.

clue.text: Assumed appearance people of either sex talked of

indicators.note: what is talked of is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: guys is now used informally for a group of men, women or both

explanation.surface: A disguise put on by men and women that everyone was discussing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked of' asks for the sound of GUYS, the informal word that now covers men and women alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outward semblance put on to conceal the truth.

clue.text: State of sailor entering Napoleon's birthplace without resistance?

indicators.note: what enters goes inside, so the sailor is placed within the trimmed island name
without means lacking, so one letter is taken away from the island

parts.note: Napoleon Bonaparte was born at Ajaccio on the island of Corsica
R is the symbol for electrical resistance in physics
tar is an old informal word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman's condition as he walks into the Emperor's home town and meets no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition but is a country. 'without' leaves COSICA, which 'entering' then splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Central American republic is one nation among many.

clue.text: Islander's triumphant cry drowned by painter

indicators.note: something drowned is swallowed up, so the cry sits inside the artist's name

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian painter of the sixteenth century
ah! is an exclamation of satisfaction on getting or finding something

explanation.surface: A native of an isle shouts in victory but an artist's noise swamps the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowned by' puts AH inside TITIAN; the 's after 'Islander' stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of one Pacific isle in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Backing American soldier, English can return fire

indicators.note: backing suggests going backwards, so the soldier's letters are read right to left

parts.note: GI is the usual term for a US serviceman

indicators.note: to return is to come back, so these two pieces together are read right to left

parts.note: a tin is the British word for a can of food

explanation.surface: With support for a US serviceman, the English are able to shoot back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns GI into IG, and 'return' turns E plus TIN into NITE. 'fire' is a verb here: to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to set something alight or kindle it.

clue.text: Cost incurred switching parts of building plan?

indicators.note: the word falls into two parts, which swap places with each other

parts.note: the layout of a building is its arrangement of rooms, its floor plan

explanation.surface: The expense run up by swapping round sections of an architect's drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching parts of' swaps the two halves LAY and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money spent, an expenditure.

clue.text: Island accommodating rodent house in the long run

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the island's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland
a rat is a common rodent
ho is an abbreviation for house, used in addresses and on maps

explanation.surface: An isle that will, given time, provide a home for a hutch of mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' reads as 'eventually', but 'in' is only a link and the definition is a literal race of 26 miles; 'accommodating' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A footrace of some 26 miles, punningly described by its great distance.

clue.text: Thing former pupil put before meeting

indicators.note: says the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, the British term for a former pupil of a school
a session is a sitting or meeting of a court or committee

explanation.surface: An item that an old school alumnus tabled in front of the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing' is the informal sense, as in 'he has a thing about trains'; 'put before' only fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: to have a thing about something is to be fixated on it.

clue.text: Sadly, one accepted an assumed name

indicators.note: what has accepted something has taken it in, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, meaning unfortunately
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Regrettably, somebody went along with a false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pseudonym someone goes by instead of their real one.

clue.text: In Russian peninsula's where you'll find a marsupial

indicators.note: in places the letter that follows inside the place name

parts.note: the Kola Peninsula lies in the far north-west of Russia, by Murmansk

explanation.surface: A claim that a pouched animal lives on a spit of land in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts A inside KOLA; 'where you'll find' links the place to what goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Australian tree-dwelling animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Trainer possibly accompanying husky, say — lucky thing!

indicators.note: accompanying means going along with, so the two pieces stand side by side
say asks for the word as it is spoken, heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a husky voice is rough and hoarse
a trainer is the British word for a sports shoe or sneaker

explanation.surface: A dog handler out with a sled dog is told how fortunate they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of HOARSE, and 'accompanying' sets SHOE beside it. 'husky' is the voice, not the dog; 'Trainer' is British footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved piece of iron traditionally hung up as a charm to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Humble dash printed in chapter head?

indicators.note: in places the printer's dash inside the churchman

parts.note: a dean presides over the chapter, the body of clergy of a cathedral
an em is a printer's measure, and an em dash is the long dash

explanation.surface: A modest stroke of the pen set in the heading of a book's section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter' is the governing clergy of a cathedral, not part of a book, and 'Humble' is a verb; the small word 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to lower someone in dignity or standing.

clue.text: Brilliant! A dealer may have one in hand

definitions.meaning: a brilliant is a gemstone cut with many facets

definitions.text: A dealer may have one in hand
definitions.meaning: whoever deals at cards may hold a card of this red suit

explanation.definitionFit: A gem cut as a brilliant, and also a card of a red suit that could be held by the person dealing.

clue.text: Called to account like a literary villain?

definitions.meaning: made to answer for one's misdeeds
a wrongdoer in fiction has been put into a novel by the author

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being made to answer for wrongdoing, read literally as being carried into a volume of fiction.

clue.text: City gent going over Mayfair church?

indicators.note: in a down clue going over suggests turning upside down, so the man's name is read upwards

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, standing for a gentleman
Mayfair is a smart London district whose postcode is W1, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A financier in a bowler hat walks past a place of worship in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns RON into NOR. 'City gent' reads as a London financier, but 'City' alone is the definition, an English cathedral town in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the county town of Norfolk in eastern England, which has a cathedral.

clue.text: Relative normality in European Community's early leaders

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each of the five words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A fairly ordinary state of affairs among the first heads of the European bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of the five words before it. 'Relative' looks like an adjective qualifying normality but is a noun, a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brother's or sister's daughter is a member of the family.

clue.text: Champion briefly imbibing a liqueur

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the trimmed word takes the letter inside
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to champion a cause is to advocate it; a champion is its advocate

explanation.surface: A title winner quickly downs a glass of something sweet and strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ADVOCATE to ADVOCAT, and 'imbibing' puts A inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thick Dutch drink made of egg yolks, sugar and brandy.

clue.text: Refrain delivered by Mercedes is tuneful

indicators.note: what these words deliver is something they carry within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A chorus sung by a woman called Mercedes turns out to be melodious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered by' says the three words carry the answer across them. 'Refrain' reads as a song's chorus but is the verb, to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to stop or hold back from doing something.

clue.text: Aga lost in travels, pining for home

indicators.note: what travels moves about, so the letters of the three words before it change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Turkish lord goes astray on a journey and longs to be back where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels' rearranges AGA LOST IN, the 'in' being part of the fodder and not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for one's own place or past, originally meaning homesickness.

clue.text: University limited by old row in greeting escapologist

indicators.note: in places the assembled middle inside the word of greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal hello

indicators.note: what limits something bounds it on both sides, so the letter sits within the two pieces

parts.note: a row is a noisy disturbance, a din

explanation.surface: A college, hemmed in by a long-standing quarrel, welcomes a famous escape artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a racket, not a quarrel or a line. 'limited by' makes OUDIN first, and 'in' then places that inside the salutation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Harry, the celebrated American performer who freed himself from chains and locked boxes.

clue.text: Signal refusal: unnerve principal of one's school?

parts.note: to unnerve someone is to rattle or unsettle them
a school's principal is its headteacher, familiarly shortened, and the possessive pronoun is kept as written

explanation.surface: Give a sign of saying no, and so rattle the person who runs the place you study at.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon divides definition from wordplay; the question mark admits that the second half is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The gesture of turning the face from side to side, which means no.

clue.text: Put into French, say, "Without one, transport's delayed"

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter that follows is left out of the word

parts.note: a train is a means of transport, so the possessive gives train's
I is the Roman numeral for one
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A request for the Gallic version of a sentence about a missing ticket holding up the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes I from TRAINS. 'say' marks French as only one example of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To render words in another language, of which Gallic speech is one example.

clue.text: Affected woman visiting Lake District's summit?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited, so the name sits within the stretch of water

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool, as in Windermere
Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: in a down clue the summit is the top, so the uppermost letter of the word before it is taken

explanation.surface: A lady deeply moved while on a trip to the highest peak in Cumbria's fells.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District, England's mountain region, is split across two pieces, with 'visiting' and 'summit' the signals; 'Affected' means artificial, not moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: artificial and stilted in behaviour or style.

clue.text: Husband quits the country, having left a will

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so the letter before it departs from the phrase that follows

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A married man emigrates after making arrangements for his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' takes H out of THE STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal term for someone who has died with a valid document disposing of their estate.

clue.text: Garden tool reportedly found under dried grass, say? Ah, well!

indicators.note: in a down clue what is found under comes lower, so the tool follows the grass
say asks for the first word as spoken, heard in another spelling

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried for fodder

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the tool's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding

explanation.surface: A gardener sighs with resignation on discovering a lost implement beneath a pile of cuttings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of HAY and 'reportedly' the sound of HOE, with 'found under' placing the second below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of weary resignation, a spoken sigh.

clue.text: Composite plant right outside church

indicators.note: outside puts the legal word round the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A daisy-like flower growing just beyond the chapel wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composite' suggests the daisy family, but here it means an organism made of a fungus and an alga living together; 'outside' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusty growth on rocks and walls that is a partnership of fungus and alga, hence made of two organisms.

clue.text: Article about an elevated stadium

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
re means about or concerning, as at the head of a letter

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means raised, so the word before it is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning a sports ground built high up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns AN into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large enclosed venue for sports or shows.
